band.basis: Working cost-plan band for one complete motorised insulated roller-shutter door, supplied, installed and commissioned into a prepared opening, GST-exclusive, NZD, Auckland. Sum of the components: low $9,040/ea, high $13,960/ea (approx $9,000–$14,000/ea). Nominal 4 identical doors on one visit, one mobilisation: TOTAL 4 doors = $36,160 low / $55,840 high (approx $36,000–$56,000), i.e. amortised access and delivery are ~$240–$460 of each door. The main cost drivers (door unit and motor) are sourced from QV CostBuilder rows with stated adjustments; the controls/safety, commissioning and delivery components are labelled allowances and together carry only about 13–16% of the total, so the band is not allowance-driven. Confidence is LOW: the door unit is a proxy (steel chain-operated slat shutter adjusted to insulated aluminium and a larger size), the two QV derivations differ, and the QV rows are unreviewed. Real NZ comparables (Attika, source-1, a 2022 guide) put a motorised 5.0 x 5.0 m steel roller shutter at $7,000–$11,000 installed, which is consistent with the order of magnitude once the insulated-aluminium premium and the smaller (18 m²) opening are allowed for.

Working cost-plan band (not a certified price) for ONE complete motorised insulated roller shutter door, 4.0m W x 4.5m H, 77mm double-skin foam-insulated aluminium slat powdercoated both faces, steel guides and full hood, 3-phase 0.75kW motor, IP54 station, safety edge and photo-eye pair, supplied, installed and commissioned into a prepared opening at an Auckland warehouse. Sum of components A-G above: low $9,900/ea, high $15,900/ea. Total for the 4-door nominal quantity = 4 x band = $39,600 to $63,600. Amortisation is auditable: the two shared items are the scissor lift (component E: $200-$800 total for the visit / 4 = $50-$200/door) and delivery/offload (component F: $600-$1,400 total / 4 = $150-$350/door); all other components are per-door. GST-exclusive, NZD, Auckland. Excludes preliminaries, margin, design, consent fees, the structural opening, the 3-phase supply/submain/isolator, and all other items listed as excluded in the scope. Confidence is LOW because the main cost driver (the insulated aluminium slat door unit) rests on a supplier 'from' price plus stated percentage adjustments for the insulated-slat and powdercoat spec rather than a published rate for that exact product, and because the QV rows used are UNREVIEWED. The band is deliberately widened; a firm supplier quote from an NZ industrial-door maker is required to close it.
